item.title: [ANALYSIS] [Publication] Competition : Law360 : Legal News & Analysis
item.description: The U.S. Department of Justice continues to build its task force targeting "gamesmanship" that it says BigLaw attorneys for major companies, especially technology platforms, are using to obstruct antitrust investigations — an effort that has been welcomed by some practitioners and questioned by others. The Federal Trade Commission set itself up for a tough fight to overturn a D.C. federal judge's rejection of its lawsuit accusing Meta of monopolizing personal social media through its purchases of WhatsApp and Instagram. Fintech company MyCard's recent complaint filed in Delaware federal court, alleging that competitor Atomic FI copied its proprietary software, including a "honeypot" in the form of a specific 37-character string, highlights fact-intensive questions of when alleged trade secrets are actually secret, says Eugene Mar at Farella Braun.

item.description: SEOUL, June 11 (Reuters) - South ​Korea will fine e-commerce giant Coupang (CPNG.N), opens new tab 625 billion won ($409.30 million) over a massive leak of ‌customer information last year and illegal collection of personal information, in the country's largest data breach penalty on a company. The Personal Information Protection Commission said the New York-listed company had leaked personal data of more than 33 million customers and failed to detect the breach within ​the 72 hours required by the law.
